intro: Kale, also known as borecole, is a hardy, non-hearting brassica grown for its leaves and young spring shoots. It used to be treated as a plain winter standby, but modern varieties give a wide range of colours, textures and flavours, from deeply curled green leaves to red and flat-leaved types. It is one of the most dependable crops for autumn, winter and early spring, often standing when little else is available, and the flavour is generally better after frost.

Kohl rabi looks like a root crop, but the edible globe is really a swelling of the stem just above ground level. It is a cabbage relative with a sweet, mild brassica flavour and a delicate texture when grown quickly and picked young. The crop matures fast, often in about 8-12 weeks, making it useful as a half-season brassica. Quality depends on steady moisture and timely harvesting: drought, checks to growth or leaving the globes too long can make them hard and woody.

Florence fennel, or bulb fennel, is a sweet, aniseed-flavoured umbellifer grown for the swollen bases of its leaf-stalks. It belongs to the same broad family as carrot, parsnip and celeriac, but is eaten quite differently: sliced raw in salads, cooked gently for a soft creamy flavour, or used in soups and ratatouille. The feathery leaves are also edible, with a gentle aniseed flavour. Modern varieties have made it easier to grow by reducing the tendency to bolt before useful bulbs form. Match the variety to its sowing season and keep young plants growing steadily: drought, crowding or root checks can give stemmy plants instead of juicy bulbs. Summer sowings after an early crop are useful for autumn harvesting. Harvest while the bulbs are tender, before they become fibrous, stemmy or frosted.

Garlic is a hardy allium grown from individual cloves, usually planted in autumn for a summer harvest. Flavour varies with the variety, from mild cloves to strongly pungent types. Young plants tolerate very cold winter weather, fit conveniently into the garden after summer crops, and are lifted early enough to be followed by French beans, late brassicas or autumn salads.
